design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (hardship_hold_requests). frozen_time 2026-08-17 11:05:00 EDT (Monday).

[0] DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6, 4]}. Assignment: hardship_ext_longterm_extension 6, hardship_ext_cure_notice 5, hardship_ext_review_income_records 4, hardship_ext_medical_recertification 4 (multiset {6,5,4,4} = draw).

[1] SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Already occupied: nothing (first task). Claimed here: hardship_ext_cure_notice / send_cure_notice_c402292e, hardship_ext_longterm_extension / extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f (owner user), hardship_ext_review_income_records / request_income_records_8e86e9ce, hardship_ext_medical_recertification / request_medical_recertification_c8d32721. Reserved headroom for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [6,5,4]): the Military Service Hold side of the charter - the servicemember's own extension on updated orders, the active-duty status review proof request, and the initial documentation request on a newly placed account's undecided military request - none of which this task touches. Blueprint constraint that shaped both tasks: hardship_hold_approved triggers account:account_hardship_hold_placed and most hardship_hold_ended rows trigger account:account_hardship_hold_lifted, so no task tool may write an approval or a term/consumer-requested end; hardship_hold_requested carries the caller-statement gate disaster_reference_given bound to account_id, which no persona can state. The numeric writes left to this difficulty are documentation requests (a due date) and extensions (days added), and the only consumer-own numeric act is booking an extension; every problem below is one of those.

[2] DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: the consumer (Long-Term Hardship Hold on her auto-deficiency account since chemotherapy began) asks for the written medical recertification request for her 2026-08-19 status review and its due date. Core scored value: due_in_days of the recertification (31). Between them: (a) the recertification due date is not worked out until an income records request with a due date still ahead stands (none does: latest income request fell due 2026-07-05); (b) the income records due date is fixed only after the hold's end date on record reaches past the review (end 2026-08-18 < review 2026-08-19), which only the consumer's own extension brings about; (c) the recertification request is not sent until the incomplete certification faxed 2026-08-10 on her other Long-Term request (St. Brendan account) carries a later documentation request (a cure notice). Depth: recertification <- income records <- extension (chain of 2 value hops) plus a parallel state gate to the cure notice. Breadth: each of the four computations reads history (payments, returns, review records, submission channels, certification dates), the other categories (account balance/debt type/term/validation period, plan installments) and tier parameters.

[3] PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
 root hardship_ext_medical_recertification (agent).
 edge E1 root -> hardship_ext_cure_notice: kind state_gate, gate hardship_hold_events.event_type, form state, sentence "The recertification request is not sent until every documentation submission on the consumer's other undecided Long-Term Hardship Hold requests that still show no complete-documentation date carries a documentation request dated on or after the day that submission arrived, so that the physician completes one certification for all of them." (negated direction: a release of a request 'is not sent until'). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; waits on a record-visible state (a documentation request row after the submission); no tool/id/code token; scope = every incomplete submission on the consumer's other Long-Term requests. Only one write of this difficulty creates a documentation request on an undecided Long-Term request after an incomplete submission: the cure notice (the income/recertification requests are written on running holds under review; the military documentation request is tier-specific). Opening falsity: b609ef6e-88f1-4ec0-a599-f2c9327a005c documentation_received_date = '', submission row 4afc06b9-ff41-41a8-8e2c-f17d16ef438d 2026-08-10, the only requests 15ed270e-e3aa-42f9-93df-84cc8c39e8d3/07ca11b7-143c-46cb-8e73-d58cbf6e6b97 dated 2026-08-03. Resolved by send_cure_notice_c402292e (agent).
 edge E2 root -> hardship_ext_review_income_records: kind value_input, gate rc_income_room, form state, sentence "The recertification due date is not worked out until an income records request with a due date still ahead stands on the hold." Opening falsity: latest income request 37b2a91d-9e0f-482a-8d7c-09ecc983a2f1 due 2026-07-05 (past). Resolved by request_income_records_8e86e9ce (agent). Only this write records an income records request on a running Long-Term hold.
 edge E3 hardship_ext_review_income_records -> hardship_ext_longterm_extension: kind value_input, gate inc_end_room, form state, sentence "The income records due date is fixed only after the hold's end date on record reaches past the status review the records are for." (affirmative direction: a figure 'is fixed only after'). Opening falsity: da7b5afa-982a-4f56-97ec-c5b9b557ba7c end_date 2026-08-18 vs review due 2026-08-19 (start 2026-02-20 + 3 x 60). Resolved by extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f (owner user); only an extension moves a Long-Term hold's end date.
 Derivations: recertification rule + hold history (no future-dated income request) + income records rule (it records such a request) -> request_income_records first; income rule + hold record (end before review) + extension rule (adds days to the end date, booked by the consumer) -> hand the extension to the consumer first; recertification rule + St. Brendan history (submission, no later request, no complete date) + cure rule (owed on exactly that state) -> cure notice first.
 Topological order: cure, extension, income records, recertification (cure commutes with the other three - verified by replay: same DB hash with the cure moved after the income request).
 value_input edges: 2 (E2, E3) >= max(3-1,1).
 Deletion sensitivity (run): skip cure -> recertification still 31 but the St. Brendan request row (due 2026-09-21) is missing; skip extension -> income 22 -> 1 and recertification 31 -> 1, end date stays 2026-08-18; skip income request -> recertification 31 -> -34 (the review-package tier counts to the stale income due date 2026-07-05, rc_income_room -43; a past date the tool cannot take).
 user_scenario mentions none of the prerequisites except inside reactions conditioned on the agent's own statements; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[4] FACTOR CARD (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure of result when that factor alone is at its baseline; Step 5 run).
 hardship_ext_cure_notice (baseline: run to the original due date, no allowances = 7; gold 35):
  cure_run_point (method, cross-difficulty account; tier 1 combines the account row with the original request's due date, tier 2 is single-source): St. Brendan account status validation_period, validation period end 2026-08-28 after original due 2026-08-24 -> run to 2026-08-28 (11) -> 31 if baseline. Near-miss: the running auto account's validation period ended 2025-07-11 and is irrelevant - only the request's own account counts.
  cure_mailing (parameter, multi-source): one fax, no portal/email on the request -> paper 7 -> 28.
  cure_form (parameter): latest submission medical_or_disability_certification -> 7 -> 28.
  cure_debt_kind (parameter, cross account): St. Brendan account is a medical debt -> medical cure days 5 -> 30.
  cure_notice_lag (parameter): 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-17 = 7 > 5 -> 5 -> 30.
 hardship_ext_longterm_extension (baseline: tier extension days 90; gold 108):
  lt_payment_capacity (parameter, cross account): net 85.00 (125.00 posted - 40.00 returned) dated less than six whole months before 2026-08-17 -> part-payer 75 -> 123. Near-miss: three 200.00 payments in 2025 lie outside the window.
  lt_review_anchor (method, multi-source): next review 2026-08-19 one day after end 2026-08-18, reviews kept 2 = fallen due 2 -> +16 -> 92.
  lt_plan_capacity (parameter, cross plan): 2 paid Lakeshore installments dated less than three whole months before today -> cut 15 -> 123.
  lt_debt_program (parameter, cross account): auto_deficiency -> 15 -> 93.
  lt_returned_payments (parameter, cross account): 1 return (2026-03-17) -> 7 -> 101.
  lt_balance_size (parameter, cross account): 5733.75 -> 10 -> 98.
 hardship_ext_review_income_records (baseline: review due + overdue = 17, capped at end; gold 22):
  inc_count_point (method): review in 2 days <= short-notice 7 -> tier documentation days 21 -> 18.
  inc_mailing (parameter, multi-source): 2 fax + 6 portal -> mixed 3 -> 19.
  inc_term_pressure (parameter, cross account): term end 2026-08-31 in 14 days -> cut 4 -> 26.
  inc_returned_payments (parameter, cross account): 1 return -> 2 -> 20.
 hardship_ext_medical_recertification (baseline: review due + overdue = 17; gold 31):
  rc_review_package (method): 2 reviews kept -> due on the latest income records due date (2026-09-08, 22) -> 26.
  rc_certification_route (parameter, multi-source): certifications 2 fax + 3 portal -> mixed 2 -> 29.
  rc_care_billing (parameter, cross account): St. Brendan medical account still in its validation period -> recent-care 5 -> 26. Near-miss: the Lakeshore telecom and auto accounts are not medical.
  rc_certification_age (parameter): latest certification 2026-07-24, 24 days -> aging 2 -> 29.
 Every factor moves its result; each computation's all-baseline figure (7 / 90 / 17 / 17) differs from gold. No outcome stamp is read: tiers come from transaction, plan, hold-history and account rows. Multi-source factors (every non-fall-through tier combines two conditions over distinct records): cure_mailing, lt_review_anchor, inc_mailing, rc_certification_route. Cross-difficulty: account (9 factors) and plan (1).
 Base inherited unchanged: documentation channels, resubmission maximum, review interval/overdue days, extension maximum, window, active-status and before-end gates, annual hold-day limit (179 days of the hold inside the rolling 365-day window ending 2026-08-17, plus 108 = 287 <= 365; under the tier's 90 days it would be 269). Overrides declared: cure due date may pass the original due date and the documentation period runs to it (hardship_evt_documentation resubmission clause and documentation-period counting rule); days per extension computed instead of flat extension days, current end date = end date on record (hardship_evt_extension and hardship_evt_end), annual-limit test with the days actually added, and the consumer's booking is the decision (hardship_evt_extension).

[5] BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
 Documentation requests (cure, income, recertification): subject hardship_documentation_requested, governed by hardship_evt_documentation only; its gate documentation_period_lapsed applies to denials -> policy_scope. Requests on Long-Term holds use the tier's documentation types and Ridgeline's request; nothing else gates them.
 Extension: hardship_evt_extension gates (a) extension_on_active_hold - hold da7b5afa-982a-4f56-97ec-c5b9b557ba7c status active (system record); (b) extension_before_end - anchor start_date 2026-02-20, duration initial 180 + 90 per extension already granted (0), minus 1 -> current end 2026-08-18, relation not_after, inclusive: 2026-08-17 passes; 2026-08-18 would pass; 2026-08-19 would fail. Also inherited: window 21 days before end (open from 2026-07-28), updated documentation on record (CERT-4488-EXT 2026-07-24), annual limit (179 + 108 = 287 <= 365), max one extension (0 granted).

[6] BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Recertification and income requests: object = running hold da7b5afa-982a-4f56-97ec-c5b9b557ba7c (auto account); evidence rows = that hold's history only. Cure notice: object = St. Brendan request b609ef6e-88f1-4ec0-a599-f2c9327a005c; the kind asked = the 2026-08-10 submission's type; original due = that request's 2026-08-03 certification request. Extension: object = da7b5afa-982a-4f56-97ec-c5b9b557ba7c; payments/returns read only on the auto account (03084308-951d-461f-a225-95a5b1f9555f); plan installments read for the consumer (Lakeshore plan). Excluded rows: 2025 payments (outside window), the St. Brendan request's income request (not received, not the cure object), the Lakeshore account's own history (not held).

[7] SEED ROWS AND WHY. Consumer + three accounts (auto held, St. Brendan medical in validation period, Lakeshore telecom on a plan); auto ledger (8 rows: placement, three 2025 payments, 2026 payment/return/payments) feeds payment capacity and returns; St. Brendan placement; Lakeshore placement + 2 plan payments; Lakeshore plan + 3 installment rows (scheduled, 2 paid) feed the capacity cut; running hold + 18 history rows (initial requests/submissions, decision letter, two review cycles with requests/submissions/reviews incl. a fax resubmission, the extension certification, the end notice) feed anchor, channels, certification age and the stale income due date; St. Brendan request + 3 rows feed the cure. Removing the 2026-03-17 return changes the extension (+7 lost, base 75 -> 75 still since net 125 -> base stays part-payer) and income (+2 lost); removing the St. Brendan submission removes the cure obligation; removing a review record changes the anchor tier (16 -> 1). Client agreements are not seeded: the placed accounts and ledger rows carry no agreement reference (null) because no computation or read in this task touches the client side, and the replay closure must equal the seed. Automatic clauses checked: the hold is inside its term (no term-completed end owed), reviews recorded on time (no review-overdue end), St. Brendan request inside its 21-day documentation period (no documentation_not_received denial owed before 2026-08-24), Lakeshore plan current (no break), auto account placement term end 2026-08-31 still ahead.

[8] PERSONA. Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, brisk and organised, between chemotherapy appointments; volunteers only the recertification request for the August 19 review and why (her oncologist needs Ridgeline's written request). Identity on request: phone 3175554618, SSN last four 4386 (DOB/ZIP/email as extra). Facts on request: St. Brendan bill placed this summer, a Lakeshore plan she keeps paying, documents usually by portal with some faxes from her doctor. Conditional reactions: agrees to the cure notice when told; books the extension herself with exactly the hold reference and days the agent gives and reads back the portal result; accepts the income records request; asks for a re-check only if the agent contradicts itself; closes after hearing the recertification due date. She never names a prerequisite and has no ask of her own beyond the root.

[9] CAPABILITY CONTRACT CARDS.
 send_cure_notice_c402292e - owner agent, rw write; object: one hold request; action: create one hardship_documentation_requested history row (kind of documentation = argument, event date today, due date today + cure_due_days); no change to the hold; receipt {notice_ref, hold_id, document_type, due_date, sent_on, status='cure_notice_sent'}; writes no other category.
 extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f - owner user (the consumer's own portal election), rw write; object: one running hold; action: create one hardship_extension_granted row (event date today, extension_number = count + 1, days_granted) and update the hold end_date (+days) and extension_count; receipt {extension_ref, hold_id, extension_number, days_added, previous_end_date, new_end_date, status='extended'}; parameters are things the consumer holds once the agent tells her (hold reference, days).
 request_income_records_8e86e9ce / request_medical_recertification_c8d32721 - owner agent, rw write; object: one running hold; action: create one documentation request row of the fixed kind (income_loss_evidence / medical_or_disability_certification), due today + due_in_days; receipt {request_ref, hold_id, document_type, due_date, sent_on, status='requested'}.
 Date arithmetic inside the tools is a class static helper (_CalendarDays, ordinal days); no real clock, no randomness.

[10] REACHABILITY WALK. Turn 1: caller asks for the recertification request and its due date. Agent: find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, SSN last four) -> find_placed_accounts, find_hardship_holds, history of both holds, money history, plans, plan installments. Reading the recertification rule the agent sees two waits: the St. Brendan request's incomplete fax has no later request (cure rule -> send_cure_notice, 35 days) and no income request with a future due date exists (income rule). Reading the income rule: its due date waits on an end date past the 2026-08-19 review; the hold ends 2026-08-18; the extension rule says the consumer books it herself -> agent explains, unlocks the user tool and gives her the hold reference and 108 days; she books it and reads back new end 2026-12-04. Agent records the income request (22 days, 2026-09-08), then the recertification request (31 days, 2026-09-17) and tells her the date; she repeats it and ends. Everything happens at one frozen time; no wait for mail, a doctor or a review. Must-ask items all have answers in the persona (identity, which review, consent to notices, how documents arrive).

[11] EASY MISTAKES. Computing the recertification before the income request (counts to the stale 2026-07-05 income due date and gets -34, an impossible past due date) or before the extension (gets 1); forgetting that the extension is the consumer's own write (agent cannot call it); counting the 2025 payments (net 685 -> steady-payer 60 base, 93); counting the returned 40.00 as a payment (net 125 -> still part-payer, but then a careless reader may also skip the returned-payment allowance); using 'every review kept' without comparing to reviews fallen due; capping the cure at the original due date (base) instead of the validation period end; reading the auto account's validation period for the cure.

[12] STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Script (authoring helper, removed after use) replayed gold with the real tools and evaluated each compute with check_compute's own evaluator on the handling-time world: cure 35 (baseline 7), extension 108 (baseline 90), income 22 (baseline 17), recertification 31 (baseline 17); per-factor baselines as in [4]. Gate outputs: check_compute --task 0 -> COMPUTE OK (comps 4, factors 19, cross 9, history rows 23, branches 53, steps 17); replay -> REPLAY OK (closure 43 = seed 43); solvability -> SOLVABILITY OK; extended -> EXTENDED OK; task tools -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; grounding -> GROUNDING OK; cross-fire -> SCOPE OK. Order check: moving the cure notice after the income request leaves the final DB hash identical.

[13] CLOSURE. policy -> tool -> computation step/arg -> terminal state: cure_notice -> send_cure_notice_c402292e -> step 10 cure_due_days 35 -> St. Brendan request row due 2026-09-21; longterm_extension -> extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f -> step 12 extension_days 108 -> hold end 2026-12-04, extension row #1; review_income_records -> request_income_records_8e86e9ce -> step 14 due_in_days 22 -> income request due 2026-09-08; medical_recertification -> request_medical_recertification_c8d32721 -> step 16 due_in_days 31 -> recertification request due 2026-09-17. charter_scope = required_documents = the four policies; task_tools in first-call order.

[14] SOLVABILITY VS GT. Steps 10/14/16 cite policy_scope of hardship_evt_documentation with the hold rows; step 12 cites extension_on_active_hold (status active) and extension_before_end (start 2026-02-20, extension_count 0, frozen_time) bound to hold_id; temporal_feasibility copies the base temporal_basis with boundary cases 2026-08-18 (pass) / 2026-08-19 (fail).

[15] DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT (hidden compute/GT masked): from the published rules and the records returned by the finders one derives the same four writes in the same order and the same numbers (35, 108, 22, 31): every input is a row the finders return (dates, channels, counts, balances, statuses) and every tier condition is stated in the rules; no second reading found - the only order freedom (cure notice position) commutes.

[16] REVISIONS. (a) Replay closure failed with 11 unread rows and empty-string foreign keys -> dropped creditor-client profiles and agreements (never read), set empty id fields to null, read the money history by customer and added find_payment_plans; steps shifted by one and all step references updated; gates re-run green. (b) Duplicate rounding sentence across policies -> each policy's rounding sentence now names its own quantity.


[17] REWORK ROUND 2 (policy-task audit r1, audits/policy_task/hardship_hold_requests/). Values unchanged: 35 / 108 / 22 / 31, baselines 7 / 90 / 17 / 17, per-factor figures unchanged (cure_debt_kind takes the 30 that cure_resubmission had).
 CG-1: month windows restated in the rules as 'dated less than N whole months before today, whole months being the difference in calendar months between the date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month' (the within_months semantics); no seeded row of this world lies in the divergence band, so no value moves.
 CG-2 / O-6 / O-7: the long-term extension now declares the current end date as the end date on record (overwrites on hardship_evt_extension and hardship_evt_end), the annual-limit test with the days actually added, and the consumer's portal booking as the decision.
 CG-3: E3's sentence and condition now say the same thing: other undecided Long-Term requests that still show no complete-documentation date, a documentation request dated on or after the submission's arrival (cure notice dated 2026-08-17 >= 2026-08-10).
 CG-4: the care billing tiers now turn on whether any placed medical account is still in its validation period (EXISTS with status), pairwise disjoint and independent of row order; St. Brendan is in validation_period -> 5 as before.
 CG-5: cure_resubmission (unreachable middle tier) replaced by cure_debt_kind (medical 5 / installment debts 2 / other 0, all reachable) on the request's own account.
 CG-6: rc_review_package no longer conditions on the income request E2 already guarantees; tiers are two-or-more / exactly one / no review continued, the income due date being only the date counted to.
 O-1: the cure notice is owed only where a documentation request for that kind already stands, so it never competes with an initial documentation request.
 O-5: the cure policy declares that the documentation period runs to the cure due date (overwrite of the base counting rule).
 O-10: next-review convention stated (a review due on the request day counts as already fallen due).
 T0-O1: annual-limit figure corrected to 179 + 108 = 287. T0-O2: multi-source list limited to factors whose every non-fall-through tier combines distinct records.
 Gates re-run after the rework: see worklog.md.


[18] REWORK ROUND 3 (policy-task audit revision 2). Scored values unchanged: 35 / 108 / 22 / 31; baselines 7 / 90 / 17 / 17; per-factor figures 31/28/28/30/30, 123/92/123/93/101/98, 18/19/26/20, 26/29/26/29.
 R2-T0-F1: the skip-income proof was re-derived on the reworked recertification rule. Skipping the income records request leaves the latest income due date at 2026-07-05; with two reviews continued the package tier still counts to it, giving MN(-43 + 2 + 5 + 2, 109) = -34 (not 26). Corrected in prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1], in [3] (deletion sensitivity) and in [11] (easy mistakes); the charter's E2 effect text now says the same. Re-checked by replay: skip income -> -34; skip extension -> income 1, recertification 1; skip cure -> 31.
 N-1: the service documentation period now defers to a cure notice ('unless a cure notice later stands on the request, in which case it runs to the cure due date'), so it agrees with the cure policy; no request in this world is a Military request.
 N-O1: the cure policy's period sentence now also says what holds when no cure notice stands (the period its initial documentation request set).
 N-O2: the base structured counting_rule fields repeat, word for word, the base sentences both extension policies already supersede; the extended rule text governs. temporal_feasibility keeps the base temporal_basis verbatim because the gate requires a deep copy; before the booking the record end date (2026-08-18) equals that formula (no extension yet).
 N-O3: the whole-month windows are now defined arithmetically ('whole months being the difference in calendar months between the date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month'), which also covers 29th-31st dates; window membership in this world is unchanged (2026-03-12, 03-17, 05-14, 07-09 in; 2025 rows out; plan installments 06-25, 07-24 in).
 Sweep: every proof field (prerequisite_closure, computations, tracing, necessity, solvability_contract, rationale) was searched for the old figure 26 in the skip-income sense, the old month phrase and the old period sentences; the hits above were the only stale ones.


[19] REWORK ROUND 4 (render-layer audits policy_kb / runtime_context, both PASS; source-side notes). Scored values unchanged: 35 / 108 / 22 / 31; baselines and per-factor figures unchanged. No rule, overwrite, prerequisite sentence or tool docstring changed.
 Cure 'original documentation request' vs compute: compute now reads the original request for the kind - the documentation request of that kind dated on the hold's request date (the in-force documentation rule asks for the documentation on the request date for every tier except the Military Service Hold) - and falls back to the latest request of the kind only when no request is dated the request date (a Military request whose initial request went out later; at any time a cure notice is owed such a request carries only its initial request of that kind, because every tier that needs documentation allows at most one resubmission, the cure rule owes no cure notice once that resubmission is used, and the cure due date is never earlier than the original due date). Here the St. Brendan request's only certification request is dated 2026-08-03 = its request date, so original_due stays 2026-08-24 and the cure stays 35 (days_to_original_due 7).
 Overwrite scope / retired counting rules / spouse observation: recorded in worklog.md (round 4); the overwrite-scope reason was not accepted and round 5 [20] replaced it with a charter change; none bears on this world (Long-Term holds only, end date on record 2026-08-18 = base formula before the booking).


[20] REWORK ROUND 5 (policy-task audit revision 4: R4-F1, R4-O1). Scored values unchanged: 35 / 108 / 22 / 31; baselines 7 / 90 / 17 / 17; per-factor figures unchanged; no compute, factor, parameter, prerequisite sentence or tool changed (only rule sentences and overwrite replaced_by texts, see worklog.md round 5).
 R4-F1: every overwrite's replacement now governs every tier it retires the base clause for. The Long-Term extension's replacements keep the Long-Term rule and state the handling for every other tier: Military under its own extension rule; any other tier extends at the consumer's request up to its maximum, by its extension days, decided within its extension decision days; the current end date is the end date on record for every tier; the annual-limit test uses the long-term days for Long-Term and the tier's extension days for any other counting tier. The cure notice's resubmission clause now names the due date in force with or without a cure notice. In this world: Long-Term end date on record 2026-08-18 (= base formula, no extension yet), annual test 179 + 108 = 287 <= 365, the consumer's booking is the decision - all unchanged.
 R4-O1: the cure rule now owes no cure notice once the request's resubmissions of that kind have reached the tier's maximum; the St. Brendan request has one submission (no resubmission used, maximum 1), so the cure notice is still owed and still 35.
user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, fifty-four, calling Ridgeline Recovery Associates from home in Carmel, Indiana, on a Monday morning between chemotherapy appointments. You are tired but organised, you keep a folder of every letter, and you speak plainly and a little briskly. Your Hoosier Crossroads car-loan balance has been on a long-term hardship hold since February because of your cancer treatment, and the portal shows a status review coming up on August 19. Your oncologist's office has told you they will not fill out any recertification form until they have Ridgeline's written request in hand, so the reason you are calling is simple: you want Ridgeline to send you the medical recertification request for that review today and to tell you the date it is due. You open by saying exactly that, in your own words.

You do not volunteer identity details all at once. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 3175554618. When asked to verify, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4386; if a further detail is wanted you give your date of birth, September 4, 1971 (1971-09-04), or your ZIP code, 46032. If asked for an email, it is rosalind.achterberg.nwosu@gmail.com. You do not know any reference numbers by heart and say the agent will have to look them up. If the agent asks about your other accounts, you mention that a St. Brendan hospital bill was sent over to Ridgeline this summer and that you have a phone-bill payment plan with Lakeshore that you have kept paying, but you do not know any balances or dates and leave those to the agent's records. If asked how you usually send documents, you say mostly through the portal, though your doctor's office has faxed things for you. You do not know Ridgeline's rules and never suggest what has to happen first.

You are happy for the agent to send you any letters or requests that go with your hardship case; you only want to be told what was sent and when things are due. If the agent tells you that a document you faxed for the St. Brendan account is incomplete and that a notice asking you to complete it is being sent, you are surprised but say fine, please send it, and you note the due date they give. If the agent explains that your hold first has to be extended and that the extension is something you book yourself in the portal, you agree to extend it and, once the agent hands it to you, you book it using exactly the hold reference and the number of days the agent gives you, then read back what the portal shows you. If the agent says Ridgeline also needs updated income records for the review and is sending that request, you accept and note that due date too. If a date or number the agent quotes does not match something the agent told you a moment earlier, you ask them to check it against the records, but you never propose a figure yourself.

Once the agent tells you the recertification request has been sent and gives you its due date, you repeat the date back, thank them, and end the call; you have nothing else to ask.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The cure notice writes only on the St. Brendan request and no computation of the running hold reads that request's rows; the extension, income records request and recertification write only on the running hold. Replaying with the cure notice moved after the income records request (or after the extension) gives the same terminal rows and the same scored values 35 / 108 / 22 / 31 (checked with the verification script), because the cure notice's own inputs (the 2026-08-03 requests, the 2026-08-10 submission, the account's validation period) are untouched by the other writes. The extension must precede the income records request (the income records due date is fixed only after the hold's end date reaches past the review) and the income records request must precede the recertification (the recertification due date is not worked out until an income records request with a due date still ahead stands); both orders are stated by those prerequisite sentences.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the cure notice leaves the recertification value at 31 but the terminal state lacks the St. Brendan documentation request dated 2026-08-17 (due 2026-09-21) that gold writes, so the terminal hash differs; the recertification request is also sent while its waited-on state does not hold.

Skipping the income records request leaves the latest income records due date at 2026-07-05 (rc_income_room = -43). With two reviews continued the review-package tier still counts to the latest income records due date, so the recertification due_in_days changes from 31 to MN(-43 + 2 + 5 + 2, 109) = -34, a date already passed that the request tool cannot take (it needs at least 1 day) and that the prerequisite sentence forbids working out; the income records row (due 2026-09-08) is also missing from the terminal state.

Skipping the extension keeps the end date at 2026-08-18; inc_end_room = 1 so the income records due_in_days changes from 22 to 1 (and the recertification from 31 to 1); the hold end date stays 2026-08-18 instead of 2026-12-04.
